text.p: (Compiled from ABC ARCHIVES, ABC RADIO NATIONAL, "On This Day" published by REED INTERNATIONAL BOOKS LIMITED, "The Chronicle Of The 20th Century" published by PENGUIN BOOKS and "Rock And Pop (Day By Day)" published by BLANDFORD BOOKS.)
BIRTHDAYS
The first child born to English parents in the American colonies, VIRGINIA DARE, was born in 1587.
Australian radical writer FRANK ANSTEY was born in 1865. At the age of 11 he stowed away on a ship from England.
Australian country singer TEX MORTON was born in 1916. American actress SHELLEY WINTERS was born in 1922. Her films included "The Poseidon Adventure" and "Lolita".

American actor ROBERT (CHARLES) REDFORD was born in 1937. His first starring role was in "Barefoot In the Park" (1967), followed by "Butch Cassidy and The Sundance Kid" (1969) and "The Sting" (1973), both co-starring with PAUL NEWMAN.

Polish film director ROMAN POLANSKI was born in 1933. His films include "Rosemary's Baby" in 1968, "Tess" in 1979 and "Bitter Moon" in 1992. He suffered a traumatic childhood in Nazi-occupied Poland and later his wife, actress SHARON TATE, was murdered by the CHARLES MASON family. TATE was pregnant with their first child. He left the United States for Europe and his tragic personal life has been reflected in his work.
EVENTS
1846 : Coolangatta on Queensland's Gold Coast was given
its name. Timber-cutters named the area after their ship which was wrecked on the beach.
1901 : A Melbourne tram was held up and passengers were
robbed in a daring bushranger-style crime.
1906 : The search for Australia's national capital site
continued with Canberra being described as "one of the most picturesque spots."
1913 : A smallpox outbreak hit Sydney. More than 600
cases were reported.
1926 : The Snowy River hydro-electric scheme to provide
water to Canberra and Sydney was first mooted.
1939 : The film "Wizard of Oz" was released in New York.
JUDY GARLAND played the lead role of 'Dorothy'.
1946 : ALBERT EINSTEIN spoke out against the use of the
atomic bomb.
1959 : The route of Britain's M1 motorway was changed to
save a forest.
1959 : The first pictures of British Motor Corporation's
new mini-car were released.
1963 : BOBBY LIMB's "Sound of Music" television show
began on Channel 9. It was intially intended as a filler show to run for only 13 weeks. It ended up being on air for a record nine years.
1964 : South Africa was banned from taking part in the
Olympic Games because of apartheid.
1967 : Boxer MUHAMMAD ALI married BELINDA BOYD, the
daughter of a member of the "Fruit of Islam". This was the karate-trained section of the Black Muslims.
1969 : British singer MARIANNE FAITHFULL took a drug
overdose while in Australia, where she was filming "Ned Kelly" with MICK JAGGER.
1969 : A Melbourne doctor announced he had performed an

abortion on a 16-year-old rape victim. Dr BERTRAM WAINER , who admitted performing three abortions, left the Australian Medical Association after receiving, what he called, a threat not to continue pushing for abortion reform. Dr WAINER also claimed 30 police were involved in an abortion protection racket.
1983 : Five people died and another 40 were injured when
a truck driver deliberately drove his road train into the bar of an Ayers Rock motel. The 36-year-old driver had earlier been involved in a dispute at the "Inland Motel". He was charged with
murder.
1986 : For the first time in Australian banking history,
the Westpac bank began selling gold bullion over the counter.
1988 : Armed with a letter from Australian Prime Minister
BOB HAWKE and four thousand cans of beer, a team of ex-Test players arrived in Beijing to introduce cricket to the Chinese.
1994 : Commonwealth Games team chief ARTHUR TUNSTALL

caused a stir and was the centre of a "media feeding frenzy" when he was reported as saying disabled athletes were an embarrassement. Mr TUNSTALL was being interviewed by a Canadian television station and he re-iterated his belief that there should be separate games for the abled and disabled athletes.
